memory_candidates.content: scripts/validate-state.sh's `--fix` block (order-preserving Check-9 duplicate repair) applies its dedup transform (`.file_scope |= (reduce .[] as $x ...)`) to EVERY project with a `file_scope` key, with no `// []` guard against a literal `null` value. On a state.json where any non-terminal project has `file_scope: null` (common -- e.g. missing-key/null-value visibility findings are a known, separately-tracked class), the general `--fix` invocation crashes with `jq: error: Cannot iterate over null (null)` and state-write.sh correctly aborts leaving the file untouched (no corruption, but no repair either). Workaround: apply the identical order-preserving dedup filter directly via `state-write.sh`, scoped to only the specific project_number needing repair (`if .project_number == N and has("file_scope") then .file_scope |= (reduce ...) else . end`) -- this is null-safe by construction since the branch never touches any other project's (possibly null) file_scope, and it is still a write through the sanctioned mutex-guarded writer, not a hand-edit. The general `--fix` bug itself is a small, separate source-store fix (add `// []` before the reduce) worth filing.

scripts/validate-state.sh's Check 8 (coarse whole-directory file_scope declaration) only WARNs when a directory entry overlaps at least FILE_SCOPE_COARSE_MIN_OVERLAP (default 3) DISTINCT other non-terminal tasks. A directory-vs-specific-file overlap between exactly two tasks (e.g. task A declares a whole directory, task B declares one specific file inside it, no dependency edge between them) is invisible to Check 8's default threshold even though it is exactly the same class of undeclared-shared-write-target risk the check exists to catch. A residue sweep using the canonical scopes_overlap_first predicate (.claude/scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh) directly, rather than relying on Check 8's threshold-gated output, is needed to surface these below-threshold pairs.
